newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close firmer, buoyed by interest in HSBC.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close firmer, buoyed by interest in HSBC.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Tuesday, helped by buying interest in HSBC Holdings Plc, and turnover also improved, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index finished up 110.73 points, or 0.90 percent, at 12,398.57. Turnover was HK$6.85 billion compared with HK$5.05 billion on Monday.
"Certainly as of a few days ago, I think the lion's share of the selling has been cleaned up," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading at HG Asia, adding that turnover was rising.
"In the afternoon, some buying interest was seen -- basically just on Hongkong Bank (HSBC Holdings)," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
The interest in HSBC Holdings came from European investors, Ng added.
HSBC rose HK$1.50 to end the day at HK$180, continuing to regain last week's losses, when it was one of the counters that bore the brunt of a market selloff after the Easter break.
"I think it (HSBC) was just oversold in the past few days. It's just catching up," said an analyst who followed HSBC, adding that the bank was still a buy at HK$180.
Brokers said the market was still staging a technical rebound from last Tuesday, when the blue chip index lost 460.13 points or 3.67 percent on the back of losses on Wall Street.
Of the property counters, Henderson Land and Sun Hung Kai Properties were slightly better, but Cheung Kong and New World were "sluggish", Ng said.
Henderson Land gained HK$1.25 to end at HK$63.75 and Sun Hung Kai rose HK$1 to end at HK$79.
Cheung Kong rose HK$0.25 to HK$65, and New World gained just HK$0.20 to close at HK$41.50.

Shares in Bank of East Asia closed HK$0.05 higher at HK$26.05 after it said mortgage applications in April had slowed following a strong first quarter which saw 20 percent year-on-year growth in mortgage lending.

Esprit Asia Holdings Ltd lost HK$0.20 to HK$3.45 on dilution fears after the fashion retailer announced it would issue 180.41 million new shares to its 71.14-percent parent, Worldwide Thousand Ltd, to raise HK$616 million.
